title: The International Space Station
examples: How many people live on the International Space Station?
What is the ISS orbiting around?
Is the International Space Station always visible from Earth?

explain.say: The International Space Station orbits Earth very high up.
It travels at an altitude of about four hundred kilometers.
The ISS completes one full orbit around Earth every ninety minutes.
Astronauts live and work in a special environment called microgravity.
One example of working in space is growing crystal proteins.
In real life, astronauts use the ISS to study human health.

faq.q: How fast does the International Space Station actually travel?
faq.a: It moves very fast, traveling about twenty-eight thousand kilometers per hour.
asks: How many kilometers per hour is the station going?

faq.q: Is the ISS always above the clouds?
faq.a: Yes, because it is orbiting so high above the Earth's atmosphere.
asks: Can you see the ISS through clouds?
Does the ISS fly above the weather?

faq.a: It means that everything seems weightless because the station is constantly falling around Earth.
asks: What does it mean to be weightless?
Is microgravity the same as zero gravity?

faq.q: Does the ISS have enough air to breathe?
faq.a: Yes, it has complex life support systems that recycle air and water for the crew.
asks: Do they need to bring all their air?
How do they breathe up there?

faq.q: How often does the ISS pass over different parts of Earth?
faq.a: Because it orbits so fast, it can view almost every part of the planet over time.
asks: Does it circle the whole world?

facts: The ISS orbits Earth at an altitude of about four hundred kilometers.
It takes approximately ninety minutes to complete one full orbit.
Astronauts experience microgravity on the station.
The station has advanced life support systems.

quiz.say: The ISS orbits Earth at an altitude of approximately:
quiz.why: This is the established altitude for the station's orbit.

wrong.0: This altitude is too low for a stable, long-term orbit.
wrong.2: This is ground level, not the space station's height.
wrong.3: This is the altitude for a different type of orbit.

quiz.say: If the ISS takes ninety minutes to orbit, what is its orbital period?
quiz.why: The time for one full circle is its orbital period.

wrong.0: This is too short to complete the full circuit.
wrong.2: This incorrectly multiplies the altitude by the time.
wrong.3: This is too long; the orbit is much faster.

quiz.say: What is the state of gravity experienced by astronauts on the ISS?
quiz.why: The constant falling motion creates a feeling of weightlessness.

wrong.0: This is the normal gravity felt on the surface of Earth.
wrong.1: This suggests a fixed, partial pull, which is inaccurate.
wrong.3: While very low, it is technically not zero gravity.
